land.text: Balıkesir, Bergama (Pergamon) and Edremit, the lands Dursun 'offered' to Orhan, taken in 1345

capitals.name: Balıkesir (later Bergama and Çanakkale)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Balıkesir Bergama' and the Anatolian beyliks table 'Balıkesir, later Bergama and Çanakkale', neither with years; Balıkesir is carried for the whole life (confidence 1 on the later seats).

correction.text: the 1305 shape (the Balıkesir region) projected back to 1296

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1305 but the Karasids 'are thought to have taken over the region around Balıkesir during the reign of Mesud II' (r. 1284-97, 1303-8) and the Anatolian beyliks table gives 1296-1357; the infobox says only 'early 14th century'. The page gives no extent, so the 1305 shape (17,614 km2: Balıkesir, Bergama, Edremit) stands in for 1296-1304, approximate. The infobox's area line names 'the region of Mysia' without a figure and lists Artaki, Pegae, Adramytion, Pergamon and Dardanellia as excluded, which the same page's capital Bergama and Dursun's offer of 'Balıkesir, Bergama, and Edremit' contradict; no km2 to compare.

Years only: unchanged shape, 17,614 km2, valid 1305-1307. 'Following the Byzantine campaign in western Anatolia allied with Catalan Company and Alans between 1302 and 1308, Karasi expanded into Lesser Mysia' (Karasids page: the expansion follows the 1302-1308 campaign, so 1308 is its earliest year, not a dated span; reviewer me-09-e) (Karasids page), so the shape widens in 1308, not in 1326 as Cliopatria has it.

correction.text: the 1326 shape: Balıkesir region plus the Lesser Mysia of the northern coast, from 1308

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Following the Byzantine campaign in western Anatolia allied with Catalan Company and Alans between 1302 and 1308, Karasi expanded into Lesser Mysia' (Karasids page: the expansion follows the 1302-1308 campaign, so 1308 is its earliest year, not a dated span; reviewer me-09-e) (Karasids page); the page names no town. Cliopatria adds about 45 cells (12,600 km2) on the north (bbox 26.3-28.7 E, 39.7-40.5 N, the Biga peninsula and the Marmara shore by my reading), from the Byzantine Empire only in 1326. The 1326 shape (30,226 km2) is used from 1308 (the end of the page's span) (bbox of the added cells 26.3-28.7 E, 39.7-40.5 N).

correction.text: the 1326 shape for 1314-1325, with the northern expansion that followed the 1302-1308 campaign

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria's 1314 shape (17,639 km2, 25 km2 more than 1305, grid noise) lacks the Lesser Mysia expansion that the Karasids page places after the Byzantine campaign of 1302-1308; the 1326 shape is used for 1314-1325.

30,226 km2 for 1326-1332: Balıkesir, Bergama, Edremit and the northern coast to Çanakkale. The page's 1328 treaty ('met with Demir Khan in Pegai in 1328, when they signed a treaty', Andronikos III) names no land. Infobox gives no km2 (the region is 'Mysia'), so no ratio.

Years only: unchanged shape, valid 1333-1345. Cliopatria ends the row in 1343, but 'In 1345, there was a change of strategy' and Orhan, 'acting as a bringer of peace' between two rival claimants, pushed the brothers into the castle at Pergamum (Orhan I page); the Karasids infobox dates the Ottoman acquisition to 1348/9 (Chronological List of 1421) or about 1335 (Aşıkpaşazade), and the Anatolian beyliks table ends the beylik in 1357. 1345 is the dated sentence.

region.text: the region round Balıkesir, Bergama and Edremit

ledger.note: 1296: Karasi Bey founds the Karasid beylik round Balıkesir. The Anatolian beyliks table gives 'Karasid Beylik | Founder: Karasi Bey | Balıkesir, later Bergama and Çanakkale | 1296–1357'; the Karasids page says the dynasty is 'thought to have taken over the region around Balıkesir during the reign of Mesud II' and dates no founding (infobox: early 14th century).

region.text: Lesser Mysia, the northern coast towards Çanakkale

ledger.note: 1302: the Byzantine campaign in western Anatolia with the Catalan Company and the Alans opens the fighting in the region; Karasi's expansion into Lesser Mysia follows it (undated). 'Following the Byzantine campaign in western Anatolia allied with Catalan Company and Alans between 1302 and 1308, Karasi expanded into Lesser Mysia' (Karasids page: the expansion follows the 1302-1308 campaign, so 1308 is its earliest year, not a dated span; reviewer me-09-e); the page names no town and mentions the Catalan Company only for the 1302-1308 Byzantine campaign.
1308: the Byzantine campaign of 1302-1308 ends; the page puts Karasi's expansion into Lesser Mysia after it, with no year (1308 is the earliest).

region.text: Lesser Mysia: the northern coast and the Biga peninsula

ledger.note: 1308 at the earliest: Karasi holds Lesser Mysia. 'Following the Byzantine campaign in western Anatolia allied with Catalan Company and Alans between 1302 and 1308, Karasi expanded into Lesser Mysia' (Karasids page: the expansion follows the 1302-1308 campaign, so 1308 is its earliest year, not a dated span; reviewer me-09-e). The year is the end of the page's span; Cliopatria draws the gain only in 1326, from the Byzantine Empire. The eu-05 dossier of the Byzantine Empire has no loss here.

region.text: Balıkesir, Bergama, Edremit and the northern coast

ledger.note: 1345: Orhan annexes the Karasid lands. 'In 1345, there was a change of strategy'; with two rival claimants to the emirship, Orhan was 'acting as a bringer of peace', pushed the brothers into the castle at Pergamum, where one was killed and the other captured; Dursun 'offered ... Orhan control of Balıkesir, Bergama, and Edremit' (Karasids page). The ottoman-empire dossier dates its gain 1346 ('1345-6').

1345: the Karasid beylik ends. The Karasids page offers 1348/9 (Chronological List of 1421) and about 1335 (Aşıkpaşazade), the Anatolian beyliks table 1357; the Orhan I page dates the annexation to 1345, the year used.

wars.name: Ottoman annexation of Karasi
wars.outcome: Orhan, as 'a bringer of peace' between two rival claimants, pushes the brothers into the castle at Pergamum (one killed, one captured) and takes the Karasid lands in 1345.
wars.note: Karasids page: 'Aşıkpaşazade dated this event to 1335'; 'The Chronological List of 1421 dated the Ottoman acquisition to 1348/9'.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary; the frontiers with the Byzantines, Germiyan and Saruhan are approximate throughout.

notes:
Row identity: Cliopatria's 'Beylik of Karasi' (Wikipedia 'Karasids', Q941887) is one state. Its row covers 1305-1343; the page ends it in 1345 (Orhan I), 1348/9 or about 1335 (the Karasids infobox) or 1357 (the beyliks table), so four dates are on the pages and 1345 is the one with a dated sentence. The start is 1296 (beyliks table); the Karasids page dates no founding.
Page budget (up to 5): Karasids, Anatolian beyliks, Orhan I; two pages kept in reserve. No page gives a km2 figure, so no ratio; the infobox 'Area' names Mysia and excludes Artaki, Pegae, Adramytion, Pergamon and Dardanellia, which sits badly with the capital Bergama and the lands offered by Dursun (Balıkesir, Bergama, Edremit); unresolved.
Not settled: where 'Lesser Mysia' lay and when the shape grew (Cliopatria 1326, the page after the 1302-1308 Byzantine campaign); the terms of the 1328 treaty of Pegai; the rulers (Karasi Bey to 1328, Demir Khan, Yakhshi Khan, Suleiman, Dursun are on the page without a dated list, so no ruler strip); the capital years (Balıkesir, later Bergama and Çanakkale, undated).
Cross-dossier: the ottoman-empire dossier gains the land in 1346 (from '1345-6'); Cliopatria's Ottoman shape holds it from 1344. The byzantine-empire dossier has no loss for the northern coast (1308 here, 1326 in Cliopatria) and no Karasid counterpart; Byzantine Cyzicus and Pegae are not recorded. The ottoman-empire dossier's neighbours list shows no Karasid event before 1346.
